title: REA Reverse – Engineer Anything
summary:
REA (Reverse – Engineer Anything) is a tool that empowers coding agents to inspect and understand how software works. It automates the complex process of reverse engineering, allowing users to ask their agent in plain English to explain program functionality, decode instructions, trace calls, and recover underlying rules.

Instead of manual investigation, REA enables agents to provide insights into applications. For example, it can determine why Windows Calculator calculates "200 + 10%" as "220" by examining the percentage handler's logic. Similarly, it can reveal the speed acceleration rules in a browser game like the Chrome dinosaur game, facilitating the rebuilding of a version with adjustable speed. REA supplies critical information like handler instructions, decompiled code, and call relationships, enabling the agent to explain findings and reproduce functionality.

REA supports inspecting various targets, including native binaries (executables and libraries), JavaScript and Electron applications, and browser and runtime activity. Setup is simple, requiring `npx rea-agents@latest setup`. The tool allows users to understand, change, or rebuild almost any software, from cloning websites to reconstructing game logic from executables.
chinese_title: REA 逆向工程一切
chinese_summary:
REA（逆向工程一切）是一款工具，它使编程智能体能够检查并理解软件的运作方式。它自动化了复杂的逆向工程过程，允许用户用简单的英语询问他们的智能体，以解释程序功能、解码指令、跟踪调用和恢复底层规则。

REA使智能体能够对应用程序提供洞察，而非进行手动调查。例如，通过检查百分比处理器的逻辑，它可以确定Windows计算器为何将“200 + 10%”计算为“220”。同样，它能揭示Chrome恐龙游戏等浏览器游戏中的速度加速规则，从而有助于重建一个可调节速度的版本。REA提供关键信息，如处理器指令、反编译代码和调用关系，使智能体能够解释发现并重现功能。

REA支持检查各种目标，包括原生二进制文件（可执行文件和库）、JavaScript和Electron应用程序，以及浏览器和运行时活动。设置简单，只需运行`npx rea-agents@latest setup`。该工具允许用户理解、更改或重建几乎任何软件，从克隆网站到从可执行文件中重构游戏逻辑。

title: A city-building game in which the city would prefer you didn't
summary:
This concept outlines a unique city-building game where the primary challenge comes from the city itself, actively resisting the player's development plans. Unlike traditional simulations, the gameplay focuses on navigating complex local politics and resident opposition.

Key elements include managing "homeowner politics" and forming "coalition politics" within "supervisor districts." Players must contend with imposed "height limits" and the delicate balance of "home values," as citizens and political factions push back against change. The game features a "day/night" cycle and provides crucial feedback and narrative through an in-game newspaper, "The Fog City Ledger," prompting players to "pause for news." This design suggests a simulation emphasizing political strategy, public relations, and overcoming entrenched local resistance rather than just efficient resource management.

title: Lobbying is corruption
summary:
The article argues that the practice known as "lobbying" in the United States is fundamentally "corruption" when viewed through a European lens. It references George Hotz's explanation: wealthy entities contribute to political campaigns (via "Super PACs"), leading politicians to enact laws favorable to their donors. Post-politics, these politicians often secure lucrative consulting roles with the very groups they aided. This process, while legally distinct from bribery in the US, serves a similar function.

The author, identifying as European, states that they understand the mechanics but would label it "corruption." This view is bolstered by Wikipedia's definition of corruption, which includes "the abuse of entrusted power for private gain" and explicitly lists "practices that are legal in many countries, such as lobbying." The article highlights Wikipedia's concept of "legal corruption," where power is abused within laws crafted by those in power to protect themselves. Ultimately, the author concludes that lobbying is a "rebranding" of corruption, differing primarily in its legality in the US and the polished appearance of the lobbyists involved.
chinese_title: 游说就是腐败
chinese_summary:
文章认为，从欧洲视角来看，美国被称为“游说”的行为本质上是“腐败”。文章引用了乔治·霍茨的解释：富裕实体（通过“超级政治行动委员会”）向政治竞选捐款，导致政治家制定有利于其捐助者的法律。政治生涯结束后，这些政治家通常会在他们曾帮助过的团体中获得报酬丰厚的咨询职位。尽管在美国，这一过程在法律上与贿赂不同，但其作用却相似。

作者自称是欧洲人，表示他们理解其中机制，但仍会将其定义为“腐败”。维基百科对腐败的定义支持了这一观点，该定义包括“滥用被赋予的权力谋取私利”，并明确列出了“在许多国家合法化的行为，例如游说”。文章强调了维基百科中“合法腐败”的概念，即当权者在他们为自保而制定的法律框架内滥用权力。最终，作者得出结论，游说只是腐败的一种“品牌重塑”，其主要区别在于其在美国的合法性以及所涉游说者的光鲜外表。

title: Telegram Desktop vulnerability allowed any user's file to be stolen
summary:
A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-107181) in Telegram Desktop versions through 7.2.8 allowed for one-click account takeover through IPC injection and arbitrary local file theft.

The exploit stemmed from how Telegram Desktop handles `tg://` links when an instance is already running. A newly launched process passes the clicked URL to the existing instance via a local socket. During this serialization, semicolons (`;`) are used as command separators. Critically, semicolons within the URL itself were not escaped, enabling an attacker to inject additional commands into the instruction stream.

These injected commands could then invoke an internal `interpret:` URI scheme. This scheme, originally intended for Telegram's internal release process, could read any file from the disk and send it to a specified chat without any user confirmation or authorization checks.

To facilitate the attack, an adversary would first add the victim to a Telegram group. They would then post specially crafted text "instruction files" (e.g., `instructions1.txt`) containing commands like `channel: <attacker_chat_ID>` and `file: <path_to_steal>` (e.g., `tdata/key_datas`). Due to Telegram's default auto-download settings for group files (up to 8 MB), these files would automatically save to a predictable location on the victim's machine (e.g., `Downloads\Telegram Desktop`). Relative paths like `interpret:../../../Downloads/Telegram%20Desktop/instructions.txt` allowed the attacker to reference these files without needing the victim's username.

Finally, the attacker would send an `https://` link (as `tg://` links within Telegram chats are handled in-process) that redirects to a crafted `tg://` URL containing multiple injected `OPEN:interpret:` commands. Upon the victim clicking this link, the vulnerable Telegram instance would execute the commands, exfiltrating the target files to the attacker's group. If the victim had no local passcode set, stealing specific `tdata` files (`key_datas`, `D877F783D5D3EF8Cs`, and `D877F783D5D3EF8C/maps`) allowed the attacker to reconstruct the session and take over the account.

The vulnerability was fixed in Telegram Desktop version 7.2.9. Users are strongly advised to upgrade. Enabling the "ask where to save each file" setting can also mitigate the risk by preventing automatic instruction file downloads.
chinese_title: Telegram 桌面版漏洞可导致任意用户文件被窃取
chinese_summary:
Telegram Desktop 7.2.8及更早版本存在一个严重漏洞 (CVE-2026-107181)，通过进程间通信 (IPC) 注入和任意本地文件窃取，可能导致一键式账户劫持。

该漏洞源于Telegram Desktop在已有实例运行时处理`tg://`链接的方式。新启动的进程通过本地套接字将点击的URL传递给现有实例。在此序列化过程中，分号 (`;`) 被用作命令分隔符。关键在于，URL本身中的分号未被转义，这使攻击者能够将额外命令注入指令流。

这些注入的命令随后可以调用一个内部的`interpret:` URI方案。该方案最初旨在用于Telegram的内部发布流程，可以在未经任何用户确认或授权检查的情况下，读取磁盘上的任何文件并将其发送到指定的聊天。

为了促成攻击，攻击者首先会将受害者添加到一个Telegram群组中。然后，他们会发布特制的文本“指令文件”（例如 `instructions1.txt`），其中包含诸如 `channel: <攻击者_聊天ID>` 和 `file: <要窃取的文件路径>`（例如 `tdata/key_datas`）等命令。由于Telegram群组文件的默认自动下载设置（最大8 MB），这些文件会自动保存到受害者机器上一个可预测的位置（例如 `Downloads\Telegram Desktop`）。相对路径，如 `interpret:../../../Downloads/Telegram%20Desktop/instructions.txt`，允许攻击者在不知道受害者用户名的情况下引用这些文件。

最后，攻击者会发送一个`https://`链接（因为Telegram聊天中的`tg://`链接会在进程内处理），该链接重定向到一个精心制作的`tg://` URL，其中包含多个注入的`OPEN:interpret:`命令。受害者点击此链接后，存在漏洞的Telegram实例将执行这些命令，将目标文件泄露到攻击者的群组。如果受害者未设置本地密码，窃取特定的`tdata`文件（`key_datas`、`D877F783D5D3EF8Cs`和`D877F783D5D3EF8C/maps`）将允许攻击者重构会话并劫持账户。

该漏洞已在Telegram Desktop 7.2.9版本中得到修复。强烈建议用户升级。启用“保存每个文件时询问位置”设置也可以通过阻止指令文件自动下载来减轻风险。

title: Nitter: Update Oct 10th seeking funding and legal help
summary:
On October 10th, Nitter developer "zedeus" issued an urgent update regarding legal challenges from X Corp. On August 24, 2026, and again on September 8, 2026, X Corp. sent cease and desist letters demanding a permanent takedown of Nitter instances and its project repository, accompanied by legal threats.

A previous update on September 7th had assured users that the project would continue with legal representation. However, zedeus now clarifies that these assurances proved untrue, and Nitter currently has no legal counsel.

The developer is now actively seeking funding and legal help to defend Nitter's future. They appeal to lawyers, organizations, and individuals who can assist, providing contact details: zedeus@pm.me and @zedeus:nolog.chat.

Donations are also requested, with funds prioritized for legal costs. Any surplus will support Nitter's ongoing development or its successor project. Multiple donation platforms and cryptocurrency addresses (Liberapay, Patreon, Ko-fi, BTC, ETH, XMR, SOL, ZEC) are provided. Further updates will be posted on the site.
